summary: Indonesia offers a Visa on Arrival — or its online e-VOA version — of IDR 500,000 for 30 days, extendable once, to citizens of 97 countries and territories, admits ASEAN neighbors and a few other countries (including Brazil and Turkey) visa-free, and requires every arrival to submit a free customs declaration online before landing.

declarations.text: All arriving passengers must submit a customs declaration online and show the QR code on landing. It is free. notes: Indonesian customs allows each passenger personal goods worth up to USD 500 duty-free; each adult may also bring at most 200 cigarettes, 25 cigars or 100 g of tobacco, and 1 liter of alcoholic drink. Excess excise goods are destroyed by officers.

The UK Foreign Office warns that possessing, using, making or trafficking illegal drugs can bring long prison sentences or the death penalty, and that all cannabis products, including CBD, are illegal. The Government of Canada notes that medicines containing morphine or codeine are controlled substances in Indonesia and cannot be brought in without prior permission from the Ministry of Health.

payments.text: The Government of Canada says credit cards are not widely accepted outside large urban centres and tourist areas, and advises carrying cash when visiting remote areas. The UK Foreign Office warns that credit card fraud is common and advises using only licensed money changers, identified by a Bank Indonesia logo and a QR code.

safety.text: Indonesia is generally safe for tourists. Watch for petty theft in crowded areas, drink-spiking and methanol-tainted spirits, and respect volcano and sea-condition warnings.

tips.text: Use only the official Indonesian immigration website for the e-VOA (evisa.imigrasi.go.id) and the All Indonesia arrival card (allindonesia.imigrasi.go.id). The UK Foreign Office says the arrival card is free and warns against alternative websites or email links that ask for payment, and against fake visa agents.
The UK Foreign Office warns that Indonesia has a zero-tolerance policy on illegal drugs: possession, use, making or trafficking can bring long prison sentences or the death penalty.
Overstaying costs IDR 1,000,000 per day; longer overstays can mean detention and deportation. Extend your VOA at an immigration office (or online for e-VOA) well before day 30.
Visiting Bali? Pay the IDR 150,000 tourist levy in advance at lovebali.baliprov.go.id and keep the QR receipt. It is separate from your visa and the e-CD.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Indonesia?
faq.answer: US passport holders can get a Visa on Arrival for IDR 500,000 (about 32 USD), valid for a 30-day stay and extendable once for another 30 days. Applying online beforehand as an e-VOA at evisa.imigrasi.go.id saves queueing at the airport.

faq.question: Can I extend the Indonesian Visa on Arrival?
faq.answer: Yes, once, for another 30 days (60 days total). E-VOA holders can extend online; counter-VOA holders apply at an immigration office before the first 30 days expire, paying another IDR 500,000.

faq.question: What is the e-CD and who must complete it?
faq.answer: Every passenger arriving in Indonesia must submit a customs declaration. It is free and can be completed from 3 days before arrival; show the QR code to customs officers when you land. Arrivals by air or sea complete it as part of the All Indonesia arrival card (allindonesia.imigrasi.go.id); arrivals by land use the e-CD at ecd.beacukai.go.id.

faq.question: What is the Bali tourist levy?
faq.answer: Foreign tourists visiting Bali pay a one-off levy of IDR 150,000 (about 10 USD) via the official Love Bali portal (lovebali.baliprov.go.id) or on arrival. It applies only to Bali province and is separate from the visa and the e-CD; check current enforcement practice before you travel.

faq.question: Who can enter Indonesia without any visa?
faq.answer: Citizens of ASEAN member states — including the Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand and Malaysia — and of Brazil, Turkey, Colombia, Peru, Suriname, Kazakhstan, Belarus, Hong Kong and Macau enter visa-free for up to 30 days. This visa-free entry cannot be extended, so anyone planning longer stays should use the Visa on Arrival (extendable to 60 days) or a tourist eVisa.
